problem: Fixed 3DGS reconstructions give realistic novel views but lack traversability, collision constraints, and verified goals, so they cannot directly serve as closed-loop navigation benchmarks. Existing pipelines need mesh repair, NavMesh construction or per-scene semantic optimization and do not scale to heterogeneous 3DGS collections.
motivation: Large collections of 3DGS scenes are becoming available and offer a scalable source of realistic environments. Turning them into reproducible navigation benchmarks needs egocentric rendering, collision-aware motion, and reachable goals in one metric frame, without building a full physics simulator.
key_idea: Keep the 3DGS frozen for RGB-D rendering and derive from it an occupancy costmap (Gaussian opacity voxelization plus height-aware projection) and training-free semantic goal candidates (multi-view SAM3 masks lifted and clustered), which together support automatic PointNav/ImageNav/ObjectNav episode generation and unified closed-loop evaluation.
insight: A coarse 2D costmap derived from Gaussian opacity is enough to act as a collision and reachability oracle: against FCL mesh queries it gives 0 motion false negatives at 0.05 m and is roughly 8-11x faster. A precision-first, training-free lifting of open-vocabulary masks gives more valid ObjectNav goals (92.25%) than feed-forward or optimization-based semantic Gaussians. The termination-sensitivity results show that distance-only SR hides last-mile failures: Stop SR stays below 0.05 for ObjectNav, and the pose criterion keeps only 49-62% of ImageNav successes.
method: 3DGS voxelization: Gaussian opacity and scale are converted to per-voxel occupancy evidence, A_v = 1 - prod(1 - rho), and thresholded by tau_occ.
Coordinate normalization: RANSAC finds the dominant support plane, which is aligned to gravity and translated to z=0. This is a rigid transform only and does not calibrate scale.

Occupancy costmap: voxels intersecting the embodiment's body height interval are projected to 2D, dilated by the agent radius, and combined with a DBSCAN plus alpha-shape support mask (unknown regions treated as blocked), at 0.05 m resolution.

Semantic grounding: SAM3 masks on rendered views are eroded, backprojected with depth, voxel-downsampled and voted (majority label, ties excluded), transferred to Gaussian centers, then clustered with DBSCAN into instance centers, kept only if reachable and collision-valid.

Episode generation: start and goal are sampled from valid cells and checked for distance, reachability, collision and semantic constraints. Expert SE(2) trajectories are synthesized and checked for clearance, heading continuity and kinematic feasibility.

Closed-loop protocol: a shared discrete action to waypoint interface, costmap collision checks, and distance-based or explicit-stop termination. Metrics are Distance SR, Stop SR, Pose SR, SPL, NE, CR, and AvgSteps.

setting.backbone: Benchmark construction pipeline: frozen 3DGS, SAM3 (open-vocab segmentation), classical geometry (RANSAC, DBSCAN, alpha-shape). Evaluated policies: LoGoPlanner, GNM, ViNT, NoMaD, NaviBridger, PoliFormer, Uni-NaVid, OmniNav, NavDP, OmniVLA.
setting.training_data: none (training-free construction); evaluated policies are used zero-shot with their released weights
setting.observation: egocentric RGB (640x480) rendered from 3DGS, plus depth for construction
setting.action_space: discrete actions mapped to relative waypoint commands (dx, dy, dtheta) in SE(2), plus STOP
setting.simulator: NavArena's own 3DGS-based simulator (InteriorGS, SceneSplat++ and 50 real captures)
setting.privileged: none for the evaluated policies; the benchmark uses camera poses and a metric-consistent 3DGS frame, and the costmap acts as the collision oracle

numbers.eval_set_note: 600 zero-shot episodes (180 easy / 240 medium / 180 hard) sampled across scene sources
numbers.method: LoGoPlanner (evaluated policy, not the paper's method)
numbers.extra: geometry-conditioned reference; PointNav success threshold 0.5 m

numbers_note: NavArena is a benchmark and its own results are benchmark statistics, not a method compared to baselines. The only entry is one evaluated baseline policy, included as a reference. The other policy scores (ImageNav, ObjectNav, multi-task) and the costmap and semantic-validity tables are not reproduced here. SR values are printed as fractions (0-1) in the paper.
results: The pipeline produces 22.2M expert trajectories (16.6M PointNav/ImageNav episodes and 5.6M ObjectNav episodes) over 2,000+ scenes. Costmap queries are 7.91x (state) and 10.72x (motion) faster than FCL with 0 motion false negatives at 0.05 m. Valid-center rate is 92.25%, versus 65.95% for SceneSplat and 57.36% for FlashSplat. In closed-loop tests, NaviBridger leads ImageNav (Dist SR 0.434), Uni-NaVid leads ObjectNav (0.374), and NavDP beats OmniVLA on both multi-task branches.
limitations: Mostly static scenes and an SE(2) motion model only, with no dynamics or physics.
Input scenes are manually screened, and rendering quality is treated as an input condition. The occupancy and semantic layers are sensitive to reconstruction and segmentation errors.

Validation is on samples (100 scenes for the costmap, 10 scenes for semantics), with no instance recall reported. Policy adaptation to the shared interface may affect absolute performance, and results should not be read as a unified leaderboard.
